---
title: "Line-up and take-off roll"
description: "How OPDI finds the moment a departing aircraft enters the runway (line-up) and the moment it starts its take-off run (take-off-roll)."
---

## In one sentence

`line-up` is the first report of a departing aircraft on the runway, and
`take-off-roll` the moment it starts to accelerate along it for take-off.

## What it needs

- A departure **runway pass** with a take-off, as described on
  [Take-off and landing times](take-off-landing.qmd#runway-pass-method):
  the reports of one track on one runway and its approach areas, classified
  as a departure.
- At least one report on the runway itself, between the two thresholds and
  within half the runway's width of its centre line.
- Evidence that the take-off started on the ground (step 1 below).

## How it is computed

1. **A take-off from the ground.** The two events are given only when the
   take-off started on the ground: the track has a report flagged on the
   ground, or slower than 50 kt, in the 60 s before the first report of the
   pass faster than 50 kt; or, when reception starts during the roll, that
   first fast report is itself flagged on the ground. A touch-and-go, a low
   approach or a track that is first received in the air keeps its `ATOT` but
   gets neither event.
2. **`line-up`** is the first report of the pass that lies on the runway
   itself (not in the approach area before the threshold). It is a received
   report; its time is not interpolated.
3. **Ground speed.** Reports on the ground rarely carry a speed (almost none
   do). Where a report has none, its speed is worked out from its position and
   the position of the previous report, when the two are at most 30 s apart.
   A report without any speed is skipped; it does not end the run.
4. **`take-off-roll`** is the first report of the first run of reports with a
   ground speed of at least 50 kt that lasts at least 5 s, with no silence of
   more than 30 s inside it. Taxiing is about 20 kt and rotation about 140 kt,
   so 50 kt separates the take-off run from taxiing; the 5 s keeps a fast
   turn-off from counting.

## Based on

- Developed for OPDI, on the runway passes of the
  [runway-pass method](take-off-landing.qmd#runway-pass-method).
- The [A-CDM Implementation Manual](../resources.qmd#ref-acdm-manual) has no line-up or
  take-off roll milestone: its off-block (milestone 15) is followed directly
  by take-off (16). The codes `T06` and `T07` in `info.milestone` are not
  the manual's numbers; see [Milestones of a flight](index.qmd#milestones-of-a-flight).
- Study: [Flight events from ADS-B, version 4](../../papers/flight-events-v4/index.html).

## What is published

Event types `line-up` and `take-off-roll`, with position, altitude,
`distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`. Their `info` holds `apt_icao`,
`runway`, `runway_bearing_deg`, `traversal_class` (`departure`), `align_deg`,
`max_gs_kt`, `milestone` and `height_reference` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Time on the runway before take-off**: `ATOT` minus `line-up`. A long value
  points to a wait on the runway for a take-off clearance.
- **Length of the take-off run**: `distance_flown_nm` at `ATOT` minus that at
  `take-off-roll`, for example per aircraft type.
- **Runway entry points**: the positions of `line-up` show which entries of a
  runway are used.

## Limitations

Both events are missing when reception starts at lift-off. When reception
starts during the roll, the events mark the first report received on the
runway, which is later than the real moment. See
[Limitations: runway events](../limitations.qmd#lim-runway).

## Availability and accuracy

No airport record gives the time of line-up or of the start of the take-off
roll, so their accuracy is not measured. The table gives how often they are
found for a recorded take-off, and their median time to the recorded
take-off, which shows they sit where expected before it.
